ShortDescription.Value: Draw an area on a hill and get a whole neighbourhood: streets that follow the contours, gentle connectors, level stepped lots, zoning, service buildings and trees. Preview it, reroll it, build it.

Publish.LongDescription:
Building on hills in Cities: Skylines II is slow and fiddly. Stepped Streets does it for you: draw an area on a hillside and it lays out a whole neighbourhood the way a careful builder would.
### What it builds
- **Streets that follow the contours**, so they stay nearly level along the hill - **Gentle connectors** that climb across the slope, never steeper than the grade you set (8 % by default) - **A connection to your nearest road** within 400 m, or a neighbourhood of its own when there is none - **Level lots stepped down the hill** with soft banks, graded before anything is zoned - **Zoning that grows**: the game's own zone cells along the new roads, as deep as each levelled lot, in the mix you choose - **Service buildings** mixed in: police, fire, clinics and hospitals, schools, parks, utilities, any unlocked roadside service building, each on a level site of its own facing the road - **Forest** on ground too steep to build, trees on the banks, optional garden walls
### How to use it
1. Click **Stepped Streets** in the bottom toolbar beside Zones, or press **Ctrl+Shift+S**. 2. Click corners on the ground; click the first corner to close the area. Drag corners to reshape, right-click removes one, Ctrl+Z undoes. 3. Pick a **layout** and **what to build**: add zones with their shares and services with how many of each. 4. The plan appears on the ground. **Reroll** for another layout. 5. Press **Build**.
**Layouts**: Contour suburb, Terraced blocks and Mountain lane follow the hill; Square, Rectangular, Irregular, Skewed and Fragmented grids suit flat or gentle ground, with **crossroads**, **staggered** T-junctions or a **traffic**-optimised through road. Untick **Shape the ground** to leave the terrain exactly as it is.
Turn on **Steep hills** for steep slopes and mountain sides. Everything else (road type, block depth, grades, lot size, grading, trees) is under **More settings**.
### Good to know
- **Ground changes are permanent**, like the game's terrain tools. **Back up your save** before a big build. - Houses grow where the city has demand for that zone. - Big areas (up to 6.4 km across) take a while to plan and lay a lot of road at once. - Early release: expect rough edges and tell me what you find.
Built for game version **1.6.***.
### Credits
Parts of the build code are adapted from **Placemaker** by jackwrichards (GPL-3.0), which in turn credits ParkManager and Grid Road Generator. Stepped Streets is GPL-3.0 too; the full source is on GitHub (link on this page).

ChangeLog.Value: - New in 2.3.0: radial layouts. Star, Rings, Spiderweb and Fan spread streets from a centre; the fan opens from the edge nearest your road. - New in 2.3.0: four more grids. Diagonal avenues, Curved grid, Warped grid and Radial grid. - New in 2.2.0: grid layouts for flat or gentle ground: Square, Rectangular, Irregular, Skewed and Fragmented grids. Pick one from the new Layout list. - New: Junctions for the grids: crossroads, staggered T-junctions, or traffic-optimised, where one through road is the only road that meets yours. - New: Shape the ground. Untick it to leave the terrain exactly as it is. - A grid lines up with your nearest road and meets it the way a real grid does, every street that runs towards it in a T. - On flat ground, the hillside layouts now point you to the grids instead of stopping. - Fixed: a new road could join yours right beside one of your junctions, so the two overlapped. Joins now keep 20 m clear of your junctions. - Fixed: some neighbourhoods next to a road with many junctions were left unconnected.
